## 1. ATH-GEM-16 · History: Kern County and the Tejon Pass, 1850-2025 (40 entries)

**Due:** 2026-12-10 · **State:** now

**Why:** Joseph lives in Frazier Park; the world history has Detroit, Malta and Lithuania but nothing about his own mountain.

**What it unlocks:** Kin, Hearth and Aether can show local history beside their own records.

**Read first:**
- Kern County's and the Kern County Museum's pages
- Tejon Ranch, Fort Tejon State Historic Park (parks.ca.gov)
- Caltrans history of the Ridge Route and Grapevine

**Do this:**
1. 40 dated events: Fort Tejon, the 1857 earthquake, the Ridge Route, Frazier Park's founding, I-5, fires and storms.
2. Same entry shape as your history files (id, date, end, precision, title, text, regions, themes, place, sources with quotes).

**Make:** `athenaeum_gemini_history-kern_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `id` (text): his-kern-YYYY-word
- `date` (text): YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD
- `end` (text or none): end year
- `precision` (text): day/month/year/decade
- `title` (text): short
- `text` (text): one paragraph
- `regions` (list): california and others from the list
- `themes` (list): from the list
- `place` (object): name, lat, lon
- `sources` (list): cite, url, quote

**Before you save, check every one of these yourself:**
- [ ] Every row has a URL you opened yourself today, on the agency's, maker's or archive's own site.
- [ ] Every quote is copied word for word from that page and is there now.
- [ ] The file is valid JSON and is named exactly as asked.

**How many:** 40

**Done when:** 40 entries.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude reads every title and date; Muse second-reads 8.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- a value without a source URL that shows it
- a quote that is not word for word on the page as served today
- a source that is a blog, forum, law-firm marketing page, reseller or AI summary where an official page exists
- rows missing to reach the count, or rows padded to reach it
- a value for a period not published yet presented as if it were (write "not published as of {date}")

## 3. ATH-GEM-18 · History: United States immigration law, 1882-1965 (25 entries)

**Due:** 2026-12-14 · **State:** now

**Why:** Kin's two crossings sit inside this history: Joseph Termenas arrived in 1912, before the literacy test (1917) and the quotas (1921, 1924); Joseph Pavia came from Malta under the quota years. The world history has the family's events but not the laws they crossed under.

**What it unlocks:** Kin's arrival stories and Athenaeum's chronicle can say which law each crossing fell under.

**Read first:**
- https://history.state.gov (Milestones)
- https://www.uscis.gov/about-us/our-history
- https://www.archives.gov
- Library of Congress

**Do this:**
1. 25 dated entries from the Chinese Exclusion Act (1882) to the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965: each law, what it changed, who it hit.
2. Same entry shape as your history files (id, date, precision, title, text, regions, themes, place, sources with quotes), with a chain (cause, event, consequence) where the source gives one.

**Make:** `athenaeum_gemini_history-immigration_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub (the desk)/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `id` (text): his-imm-YYYY-word
- `date` (text): YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD
- `precision` (text): day/month/year
- `title` (text): short
- `text` (text): one paragraph
- `regions` (list): usa and others
- `themes` (list): law, migration ...
- `sources` (list): url + quote each
- `chain` (object or null): cause, event, consequence

**Before you save, check every one of these yourself:**
- [ ] Every row has a URL you opened yourself today, on the agency's, maker's or archive's own site.
- [ ] Every quote is found with Ctrl+F on that page, word for word.
